question: Who was the first official World Chess Champion, winning the title in 1886?
fact: Steinitz beat Johannes Zukertort in 1886 and held the title until Lasker won it in 1894.

question: Garry Kasparov held the world chess title from 1985 until which year?
fact: Kasparov lost the title to Vladimir Kramnik in London in 2000.

question: In which city was the 1972 world chess match between Fischer and Spassky held?
fact: Bobby Fischer won the match, becoming the first American world chess champion.

question: In algebraic chess notation, which letter stands for the queen?
fact: The king is K, so the knight is written N to avoid confusion.

question: Chess ratings are named after which Hungarian-American physics professor?
fact: FIDE adopted the Elo rating system for chess players in 1970.

question: What is the Chinese name for the board game Go?
fact: Go comes from the Japanese word go; Baduk is the Korean name for the same game.

question: What is the Korean name for the board game Go?
fact: Janggi is a Korean board game, a close relative of Chinese xiangqi.

question: Which sowing game, played in pits with seeds, takes its name from an Arabic word meaning 'to move'?
fact: Mancala-style games have been played across Africa, Asia and the Americas for centuries.

question: How many numbered suits are there in a standard mahjong set?
fact: The three numbered suits are characters, bamboo and circles (dots).

question: In shogi, what can a player do with a piece they have captured?
correct: Drop it back onto the board
fact: Captured shogi pieces change sides and can later be dropped by their new owner.

question: In shogi, a pawn that reaches the last rank is promoted into which piece?
fact: A promoted pawn, the tokin, moves exactly like a gold general.

question: Which ancient Egyptian board game is considered an ancestor of backgammon?
fact: Senet boards from Egypt date back to around 3000 BCE.

question: Emperor Akbar of the Mughal Empire was a famous player of which board game?
fact: Akbar reportedly played pachisi on a huge courtyard board using people as living pieces.

question: How many tokens does each player have in the game of Ludo?
fact: Each Ludo player races four tokens from base to home.

question: Carrom, played by flicking discs into pockets, is most popular in which part of the world?
fact: Carrom is especially popular in India, Pakistan, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka.

question: How many pockets does a standard carrom board have?
fact: A carrom board has one pocket at each of its four corners.

question: How many players form two partnerships in the card game Bridge?
fact: Partners sit opposite each other across the table.

question: How many cards does each player hold in a standard bridge deal?
fact: All 52 cards are dealt, 13 to each of the four players.

question: In two-player cribbage, how many cards is each player dealt?
fact: Each player keeps four cards and passes two into the crib.

question: How many tableau columns does Klondike solitaire start with?
fact: The first column holds one card and the seventh holds seven.

question: Roughly how many possible positions does a standard 3x3 Rubik's Cube have?
fact: The exact count is 43,252,003,274,489,856,000 positions.

question: In which year did the Rubik's Cube first go on sale?
fact: Rubik first called his creation the Magic Cube.

question: Which Japanese publisher helped popularise the number puzzle Sudoku in the 1980s?
fact: Sudoku was first published in 1979 in an American puzzle book, under the name Number Place.

question: Who published the first modern crossword puzzle in 1913?
fact: Wynne's puzzle ran in the New York World, where it was called a word-cross.

question: The seven-piece tangram puzzle originated in which country?
fact: In Chinese, tangram pieces are called the seven boards of skill.

question: Azul, a tile-laying game, takes its theme from the ceramic tiles of which country?
fact: Azulejo tiles decorate many buildings across Portugal.

question: The game Wingspan, designed by Elizabeth Hargrave, is themed around what?
fact: Wingspan was published in 2019 and won the Kennerspiel des Jahres award.

question: What kind of images appear on the cards of the picture game Dixit?
fact: Dixit, designed by Jean-Louis Roubira, won the Spiel des Jahres in 2010.

question: Which 13-year-old player beat Donald Byrne in the 1956 'Game of the Century'?
fact: The game was played in New York, and Fischer was 13 years old at the time.

question: Viswanathan Anand, a five-time world chess champion, is from which country?
fact: Anand was world champion from 2007 to 2013.

question: Which professional Go player lost 4-1 to DeepMind's AlphaGo in 2016?
fact: The 2016 match was played in Seoul, South Korea.

question: Who won the 1948 world chess championship tournament after Alekhine's death?
fact: Botvinnik was the Soviet champion who went on to hold the title for much of the 1950s.

question: In mahjong, how many identical tiles make up a 'pong'?
fact: A pong is three identical tiles; a kong uses four.

question: In which year did Parker Brothers publish the board game Monopoly?
fact: Parker Brothers bought Charles Darrow's version of the game and published it in 1935.

question: In English draughts, what is a piece called once it reaches the far side?
fact: A draughts king can move backward as well as forward.

question: In backgammon, what is the cube called that is used to double the stakes?
fact: The doubling cube is marked 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 and 64.

question: How many tiles are in a standard double-six dominoes set?
fact: A double-six set has one tile for every pair of numbers from zero to six.

question: In Chinese chess (xiangqi), what is the name of the king-equivalent piece?
fact: Xiangqi pieces include advisors, elephants, horses, chariots, cannons and soldiers.

question: In standard Ludo, what roll is needed to bring a token out of its base?
fact: In standard Ludo rules a six is needed to release a token from its base.

question: How many pieces does each player start with in shogi?
fact: Each shogi side starts with 20 pieces, including nine pawns.

question: Hive, a two-player abstract game, is played with what kind of pieces?
fact: Hive's tiles picture insects, and each tile is a hexagon.

question: Which chess opening starts with 1.d4 and 2.c4, offering a pawn to gain the centre?
fact: Black can often decline the offered c-pawn, and the opening is one of chess's most studied.

question: A draw can be claimed when the same chess position occurs three times. What is this rule called?
fact: The same player must be to move in each of the three occurrences of the position.

question: What is the chess term for a position where every legal move makes the side's position worse?
fact: Zugzwang comes from German and means roughly compulsion to move.

question: In chess, what is a move called when one piece attacks two enemy pieces at once?
fact: Knights are the pieces most often used to fork, since they jump over others.

question: How many squares can a knight reach from the centre of an empty chessboard?
fact: A knight in the middle of an empty board has eight possible destination squares.

question: In standard piece values, how many points is a knight worth?
fact: A bishop is also worth three points, and a rook five.

question: Which chess grandmaster wrote the influential 1925 book 'My System'?
fact: My System explained the idea of overprotecting key squares and pieces.

question: Vera Menchik, a player from Russia and England, won the first Women's World Chess Championship in what year?
fact: Menchik won the first Women's World Championship in 1927 and held the title until her death in 1944.

question: In Go, which colour of stone traditionally moves first?
fact: White receives komi, extra points, to compensate for moving second.

question: In Go, what is 'komi'?
incorrect: A stone placed on the edge
fact: Japanese rules use a komi of 6.5 points, so White can never tie.

question: Which Go rule stops an immediate recapture that would repeat an earlier board position?
fact: A ko is a shape where a recapture would immediately repeat the position.

question: In Go, what does a player call 'atari' to warn their opponent?
fact: Atari is a Japanese word that has also entered English through Go and video games.

question: Which shogi piece moves only forward, in an L-shape, like a chess knight that cannot go back?
fact: The shogi knight can only jump forward, unlike the chess knight.

question: How many decks of cards are typically shuffled together for the game Canasta?
fact: Canasta uses two standard decks and includes jokers as wild cards.

question: In baccarat, how many points is a king worth?
fact: Tens and face cards all count as zero in baccarat.

question: In Crazy Eights, which card can be played on any other card whatever its suit?
fact: Playing an eight lets the player name the suit the next player must follow.

question: Skat, a three-player trick-taking card game, comes from which country?
fact: Skat is played with a 32-card deck, from the sevens up to the aces.

question: In Uno, what word must a player call when they are down to one card?
fact: Uno is the Spanish and Italian word for the number one.

question: Craps, a dice game popular in casinos, is played with how many dice?
fact: Craps uses two six-sided dice, and the total of both dice decides each roll.

question: In the game Splendor, what do players collect to buy development cards?
fact: Splendor was designed by Marc Andre and published in 2014.

question: The Codenames word grid is how many cards in total?
fact: The Codenames grid is five cards by five cards.

question: Diplomacy, the negotiation game set in pre-war Europe, has how many great powers?
fact: The seven powers include Austria-Hungary, Russia and Turkey.

question: In the game Quoridor, what do players place on the board to slow their opponent?
fact: Quoridor's walls block paths, so players must find a longer way round.

question: In 1997 which computer chess machine defeated Garry Kasparov in a six-game match?
fact: Deep Blue won the match 3.5 to 2.5, the first time a machine beat a reigning champion.

question: Which chess opening begins 1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4?
fact: The Italian Game is one of the oldest openings studied in chess books.

question: The French Defence begins with which pair of moves?
fact: The French Defence often leads to a closed, strategic battle in the centre.

question: The 15 puzzle slides numbered tiles inside a frame of how many squares?
fact: The 15 puzzle caused a craze in the United States in 1880.

question: Who published the Tower of Hanoi puzzle in 1883 under a pseudonym?
fact: Lucas published the puzzle under a made-up name, N. Claus de Siam.

question: What is the minimum number of moves needed to solve the Tower of Hanoi with three disks?
fact: The minimum is 2 to the power of n minus 1, so three disks need seven moves.

question: Which puzzle uses row and column number clues to reveal a hidden picture?
fact: Nonograms are also called Picross, a name used by a Nintendo game series.

question: How many suits, one for each month, does the Japanese card game Hanafuda have?
fact: The 48 Hanafuda cards are grouped into 12 suits of four cards each.

question: The word checkmate comes from a Persian phrase meaning what?
fact: The Persian phrase shah mat is the origin of the English word checkmate.

question: Which 18th-century chess 'automaton' was operated by a hidden person inside its cabinet?
fact: Wolfgang von Kempelen built the Turk in 1770, and it toured Europe for decades.

question: Euchre is played with a deck of how many cards?
fact: Euchre uses the nines through aces of each suit.

question: In the card game Hearts, which card is worth 13 penalty points?
fact: Each heart is worth one point, and the Queen of Spades is worth 13.

question: Standard sudoku puzzles use a grid of how many squares along each side?
fact: Standard sudoku has nine rows, nine columns and nine boxes of three by three.

question: The Soma cube puzzle is made of how many pieces?
fact: The Soma cube was invented by Piet Hein, and its seven pieces make a three-by-three cube.

question: Chess960, a variant with randomised starting positions, was promoted by which former world champion?
fact: Fischer announced the idea of random starting positions in 1996.

question: In Spanish, what is the chess rook called?
fact: Torre means tower; caballo is the knight and alfil is the bishop.

question: There are 12 distinct pentominoes, each made from how many squares?
fact: Each pentomino joins five equal squares edge to edge.

question: Which word game, changing one letter at a time, was invented by Lewis Carroll?
fact: Carroll published Doublets in 1879; it is also called word ladder.

question: In the 2010 card game 7 Wonders, what do players build over three ages?
fact: 7 Wonders was designed by Antoine Bauza and published in 2010.

question: The board game Blokus is played with pieces made of what shape?
fact: Blokus was invented in 2000 by Bernard Tavitian.

question: Snakes and ladders is descended from an Indian game that taught what?
fact: The Indian ancestor, Moksha Patam, was a teaching board about good and bad deeds.

question: In English Scrabble, how many points is the letter J worth?
fact: J and X are each worth eight points in English Scrabble.

question: In Yahtzee, how many points is a Yahtzee (five of a kind) worth in its own box?
fact: Each further Yahtzee roll after the first earns a bonus of 100 points.

question: Connect Four was launched in 1974 by which toy company?
fact: Connect Four was first released by Milton Bradley and became a classic family game.

question: The game Operation, with its tweezers challenge, was released in which year?
fact: In Operation, players remove plastic pieces without touching the edges of the holes.

question: The Nihon Ki-in is the governing association of which game in Japan?
fact: The Nihon Ki-in is Japan's central body for professional Go and its rules.

question: Which organisation governs world chess and runs the Chess Olympiad?
fact: FIDE is the World Chess Federation, founded in Paris in 1924.

question: Dominion, the game that started the deck-building craze, was released in which year?
fact: Donald X. Vaccarino designed Dominion, in which players buy cards to build a deck.

question: How many faces does a standard Rubik's Cube have?
fact: Each face of a standard Rubik's Cube has nine stickers.

question: Gomoku, the game of five in a row, has a Japanese name meaning what?
fact: In gomoku, players win by placing five of their stones in a straight line.

question: A standard tarot deck contains how many cards?
fact: A tarot deck has 22 trump cards and 56 suit cards.

question: In Texas Hold'em, what is the name of the fifth and final community card?
fact: The fourth community card is called the turn.

question: Hex, a connection game on a board of hexagons, was invented by which Danish polymath in 1942?
fact: Hex can never end in a draw, because one player always connects their sides.

question: The Korean card game Go-Stop is played with a deck called what?
fact: Hwatu cards are related to the Japanese hanafuda deck.

question: Chinese checkers is descended from a German game first marketed in which year?
fact: The German game was called Sternhalma, and the Chinese name came later.

question: The peg solitaire board in its traditional English layout has how many holes?
fact: The traditional layout is a cross shape with 33 holes and one peg missing at the start.

question: In the card game Sushi Go!, what do players draft?
fact: Players draft cards from a shared pack and try to make the best set of dishes.

question: How many cards are in a standard Dobble deck?
fact: Each Dobble card shows eight symbols, and any two cards share exactly one symbol.

question: In the card game Mao, what is secret from new players?
fact: Players learn the rules only by playing, because they are never fully explained.

question: How many triangles make up a standard tangram set?
fact: A tangram set has five triangles, one square and one parallelogram.

question: Henry Dudeney's famous puzzle turns an equilateral triangle into what shape?
fact: Dudeney's solution uses just four pieces cut from the triangle.

question: The chess capture 'en passant' is French for what?
fact: En passant is the only chess capture where the captured piece is not on the square it lands on.

question: In Japanese mahjong, what does a player declare when their hand is one tile from winning?
fact: Riichi is declared with a closed hand, which then cannot be changed.

question: The Hoogovens chess tournament, held since 1938, takes place in which Dutch village?
fact: Wijk aan Zee is a seaside village on the North Sea coast.

question: Which country awards the Spiel des Jahres prize for board games?
fact: The award was first given in 1979 and is one of the best-known board game prizes.

question: How many ways are there to place eight non-attacking queens on a chessboard?
fact: Removing rotations and reflections leaves exactly 12 fundamental solutions.

question: The card game Set uses a deck of how many unique cards?
fact: Each Set card has four attributes, each with three possible values.

question: In Chinese mahjong, the three dragon tiles are which colours?
fact: The dragon tiles are red, green and white, and each is a separate honour tile.

question: How many dice are used in the word game Boggle?
fact: Boggle's sixteen lettered dice sit in a four-by-four tray.

question: Fanorona, a strategy game of captures, is considered the national game of which country?
fact: Fanorona is played on a board of 45 intersections with a capture rule that can pull pieces back.

question: Bagh-Chal, a traditional asymmetric hunting game, comes from which country?
fact: Bagh-Chal pits four tigers against twenty goats on a five-by-five grid.

question: The Royal Game of Ur was named after a city in which modern-day country?
fact: Ur was a Sumerian city, and boards of the game were found in its royal tombs.

question: How many wind tiles are in a standard mahjong set?
fact: There are four wind tiles of each of the four winds: east, south, west and north.

question: In Chinese checkers, how many marbles does each player use?
fact: Each player places ten marbles in one point of the six-pointed star.

question: Hnefatafl, a game of a king escaping to the corners, comes from which region?
fact: In most rule sets, the king wins by reaching one of the board's corners.

question: Rummikub tiles come in how many colours?
fact: Rummikub has 104 numbered tiles plus two jokers, in black, red, blue and yellow.

question: The board game Twilight Struggle recreates which conflict?
fact: Twilight Struggle covers the period from 1945 to 1989 in a two-player game.

question: In the dice game Farkle, how many dice are used?
fact: A roll with no scoring dice is called a farkle, and the player loses their turn.

question: In the puzzle Kakuro, what do the numbers in the black cells represent?
correct: Sums of the cells in a run
fact: Kakuro is a cross-sum puzzle, often called a Japanese crossword.

question: How many squares does a standard tic-tac-toe grid have?
fact: With perfect play from both sides, tic-tac-toe always ends in a draw.

question: Kriegspiel, a chess variant, hides what from each player?
fact: A referee announces captures and checks, but never reveals where the hidden pieces stand.

question: Which chess tactic attacks a valuable piece that must move, exposing a less valuable piece behind it?
fact: A skewer is like a reversed pin: the valuable piece stands in front.

question: In chess, what is a discovered check?
fact: The piece that moved can also create a second threat at the same time.

question: The first international chess tournament, in 1851, was held in which city?
fact: Adolf Anderssen won the 1851 London tournament, which launched international chess.

question: In chess, castling is illegal when the king is in which situation?
fact: The king also may not pass through a square that is under attack when castling.

question: In Go, what is a 'seki' position?
fact: In seki, neither group can be captured because they share their last liberties.

question: How many eyes, or separate empty points, must a group have to live in Go?
fact: A group with two separate eyes can never be captured.

question: How many star points, called hoshi, are on a standard 19x19 Go board?
fact: Hoshi are marked points that help players judge the shape of the position.

question: In Go, what is 'sente'?
correct: A move that forces a reply
fact: Gote is the opposite: a move that does not force the opponent to answer.

question: In mahjong, what is a chow?
correct: Three in a row, one suit
fact: A chow can only be formed from tiles of a numbered suit, never from honour tiles.

question: Traditional mahjong is played by how many players?
fact: Most mahjong variants are played by four players seated at a square table.

question: Which chess piece has no direct equivalent in standard shogi?
fact: Shogi's rook and bishop combine many of the queen's moves between them.

question: Pinochle is traditionally played with a deck of how many cards?
fact: A pinochle deck contains two copies of each card from nine to ace in every suit.

question: In rummy, what is a run?
fact: A run is usually three or more consecutive cards of the same suit.

question: In bridge, what is the name for winning all 13 tricks?
fact: Winning twelve tricks is called a small slam.

question: Belote, a trick-taking card game for pairs, is especially popular in which country?
fact: Belote is played in partnerships, with a trump suit and a bonus for holding the king and queen.

question: The ancient race game Game of the Goose has how many squares on its track?
fact: Landing on a goose square lets a player move forward again on the next roll.

question: In nine men's morris, how many pieces does each player have?
fact: The board was carved into stone seats and cathedral floors across medieval Europe.

question: In the game Sorry!, how many pawns does each player move?
fact: Players use a deck of cards to decide how far each pawn moves.

question: Slitherlink, a Japanese logic puzzle, asks the solver to draw what?
fact: The numbers in the cells show how many sides of each cell the loop uses.

question: Which chess writer and champion published the 1921 classic 'Chess Fundamentals'?
fact: Capablanca was world champion from 1921 to 1927.

question: Judit Polgar, one of the strongest players ever, is from which country?
fact: Polgar became a grandmaster at the age of 15 in 1991.

question: Which of these is one of the four central squares of a chessboard?
fact: The four central squares are d4, d5, e4 and e5.

question: The Italian card game scopa is named after the Italian word for what?
fact: In scopa, a player who clears the whole table earns a sweep, which is also a broom.

question: In a standard tarot deck, which card is numbered zero?
fact: The Fool is often placed first or last in the sequence of the 22 trump cards.

question: Mastermind, the code-breaking game, was invented in 1970 by a telecoms expert from which country?
fact: Mordecai Meirowitz invented Mastermind, which was based on an earlier pencil-and-paper game.

question: How many numbered tiles are in the classic 3x3 sliding puzzle?
fact: Half of all possible starting arrangements of the 8 puzzle cannot be solved.

question: The French name for the game of draughts is what?
fact: Draughts is called checkers in the United States, and played on an eight-by-eight board.

question: How many blank tiles does an English Scrabble set contain?
fact: A blank tile can stand for any letter and scores zero points.

question: In Monopoly, how many houses must be built on a property before a hotel can go on it?
fact: Once four houses are built, the owner can upgrade the property to a hotel.

question: In Monopoly, rolling three doubles in a row sends a player where?
fact: Three consecutive doubles send the player straight to Jail.

question: Howard Staunton's name is attached to the standard design of which game pieces?
fact: The Staunton design became the standard for tournament chess pieces.

question: In the 1957 Swedish film The Seventh Seal, a knight plays chess against whom?
fact: The film was directed by Ingmar Bergman and is one of the most famous chess scenes in cinema.

question: Stefan Zweig's novella about a chess match on a transatlantic ship is called what?
fact: The Royal Game was published in 1942, the year Zweig died.

question: In Nurikabe, a Japanese logic puzzle, what must form one connected region?
fact: In Nurikabe, the black cells may not form any two-by-two block.

question: In the classic Kalah game, how many pits does each side have?
fact: Each Kalah pit starts with four seeds, so each side begins with 24.

question: In Go, what is an 'eye' of a group?
fact: A group needs two separate eyes to stay alive for good.
